answer: New identities enter an activation queue that admits only 20 per epoch network-wide, and each entrant must lock 35 POA for 14 epochs. A velvet-rope queue means 1,000 fakes wait 50 epochs and lock 35,000 POA, while an honest agent waits at most one epoch and locks 35 once. Each signal an agent emits is spot-checked: auditors replay 9% of tasks, and a mismatch slashes 60% of the lock. Even a nebula of 200 fakes costs 7,000 POA and 10 epochs of waiting, so cost grows linearly in N.
